findings.claim: The done criterion "the result passes the okf validator" rests on a validator kmctl's tests cannot reach as the plan stands. The validator is okf_validate.py from the okf plugin (scaccogatto/okf-skills); here it exists only in ~/.claude/plugins/cache/scaccogatto/okf/0.10.1/skills/validate/scripts/, and it is not a kmctl dependency (pyproject lists only typer). It is a PEP 723 script needing pyyaml, so `uv run` fetches pyyaml at run time. The tests gate (`uv run pytest`) and CI have no defined way to run it. The obvious workarounds change the contract: vendoring the script goes against ADR 0003 ("Copy the okf skills into kmctl. Two copies drift."); skipping the check when the plugin is missing makes the criterion silently optional; a check re-implemented in kmctl is not "the okf validator". The plan must say how the test gets the validator (for example fetched from a pinned okf-skills ref, or the okf GitHub Action in CI) and whether it runs in strict mode. Spike question: can a pytest test under `uv run pytest` in this repo's gate environment run okf_validate.py from a pinned source, with no plugin installed under ~/.claude, and pass a scaffolded bundle?

The plan did not say how kmctl's tests reach the okf validator. It now names a pinned, test-only copy of okf_validate.py from okf-skills 0.10.1 under tests/vendor/ with its MIT licence, run in strict mode, with pyyaml as a dev dependency.
